If $m=1$, then $D$ is the star with center $x_1$ and leaves $b,c,d$. The center is adjacent to both $u,v$, or to one of them while one of $b,c,d$ is adjacent to the other. If $m=2$, the degrees of $x_1,x_2$ in $D$ sum to four, so both have degree two. Their neighborhoods in $\{b,c,d\}$ meet in one vertex and together contain all three. Thus $D$ is the path $g_1x_1g_2x_2g_3$ for some ordering $g_1,g_2,g_3$ of $b,c,d$. The vertices $x_1,x_2$ are adjacent to different vertices of $\{u,v\}$, or both are adjacent to one and one of $b,c,d$ is adjacent to the other. These choices give the $31$ forms checked in~\supp{E11}, leaving exactly $\mathfrak T_{40},\mathfrak T_{53},\mathfrak T_{56},\mathfrak T_{73}$.
\end{proof}

vertex names: Psi_2 with twins p, q on {a, b, c} and r, z on {a, b, d}, as in Section 5. The bridge B has attachments a, b, c, d and contains u, v and the twins p', q' with neighbourhood X = {a, u, v}. The vertices of M are m (star) or m1, m2 (path g1 m1 g2 m2 g3).
the forms: One component D of B - X contains b, c, d, with N_B(D) = {u, v}. Its bipartite tree is a star whose centre m is joined to b, c, d, or a path g1 m1 g2 m2 g3 with {g1, g2, g3} = {b, c, d}. For the star, m meets both u, v, or one of them and a vertex of {b, c, d} meets the other. For the path, m1, m2 meet different vertices of {u, v}, or both meet one and a vertex of {b, c, d} meets the other. Up to symmetry this gives 31 forms.
the four tests: Lemma 5.3 with (n_c, n_d) = (2, 2): G is toroidal if and only if one of B + ac + bd, B + ad + bc, B + ab + ac + ad, B + ab + bc + bd is planar.
